title: Kyler Murray ruled out of Vikings debut, in concussion protocol after violent collision
content:
MINNEAPOLIS — Minnesota Vikings quarterback Kyler Murray exited Sunday’s game in the first quarter after taking a hit to the head and went directly to the locker room. The Vikings ruled him out for the rest of the game and said he is in the concussion protocol.

On Minnesota’s third possession, Murray scrambled on a third-and-7 play. Green Bay Packers edge rusher Lukas Van Ness and defensive back Javon Bullard collided with Murray as he went to the ground. Immediately, Murray lay on the ground, and the Vikings’ trainers trotted out to check on him.

Green Bay was penalized for unnecessary roughness.

The Vikings replaced him with backup quarterback Carson Wentz, and Murray bypassed the medical tent to head straight to the locker room.

Minnesota’s offense struggled during its first two drives with Murray at the helm. He threw an interception on his first pass attempt in the face of pressure from the Packers. On the team’s second possession, two false starts doomed any offensive momentum. Murray ended up 3-for-5 passing for 18 yards.

This story will be updated.
